title: Create supported_onchain_rwa_securities function in rwa module
Replace NVIDIA buffered runtime with a first-class streaming subsystem
description:
Supersede the current NVIDIA-specific buffered mitigation path with one stream-aware subsystem for direct and smart-alias NVIDIA execution. The new subsystem must own transport policy, SSE parsing, keepalive behavior, meaningful-output lock-in, retry suppression after output begins, and inference-backed health.

This epic exists because the current implementation still reasons about NVIDIA primarily through buffered completions and deadline timers rather than chunk-aware streaming state. That is structurally too weak for long silent reasoning gaps, streaming correctness, and safe smart-alias racing.
design: Use a replacement sequence, not additive layering: build primitives, cut over direct NVIDIA, cut over smart-alias NVIDIA, add inference-backed health, then delete the legacy buffered path.
acceptance_criteria:
A single NVIDIA streaming subsystem materially replaces the legacy buffered runtime path for direct and smart-alias NVIDIA handling.
Direct and smart-alias NVIDIA use the same parser and stream-state machinery.
Retry and hedge are impossible after meaningful output begins.
Legacy buffered NVIDIA runtime code is removed or inactive.

title: Build NVIDIA stream primitives and SSE parser
description:
Create the new foundation for NVIDIA streaming: chunk-aware parser, stream engine state, and sink abstraction.

This bead owns the low-level pieces that the later cutovers depend on. It should not switch runtime authority yet, but it must be strong enough that direct and smart-alias NVIDIA can move onto it without reintroducing buffering assumptions.
design: Keep routing authority in ThinkingProxy, but move transport-independent streaming mechanics out of the giant file. The goal is a reusable engine for both buffered and streamed sinks.
acceptance_criteria:
Introduce dedicated NVIDIA stream primitives in new source files.
Parser handles partial frames, comments, data frames, [DONE], UTF-8 failure, and oversized-frame rejection.
Engine tracks first-byte, last-chunk, terminal, and meaningful-output state.
No runtime cutover yet.

title: Define meaningful-output lock-in and post-output retry suppression
description:
Specify and implement the state transition that makes NVIDIA streaming safe under retries and races. Once meaningful output begins, the active lane owns the request and all retry or hedge behavior must stop.

This bead covers the semantic boundary, not the transport itself.
design: Do not scatter this policy through ThinkingProxy callbacks. It belongs in the stream engine state machine so all NVIDIA execution surfaces inherit the same rule.
acceptance_criteria:
The stream engine exposes a meaningful-output transition for text, tool-call, and responses output forms.
After that transition, retries and hedges are impossible.
The behavior is verified for both direct and smart-alias paths via shared engine tests.

title: Cut direct NVIDIA requests over to the new streaming engine
description:
Switch the direct NVIDIA runtime path off the legacy buffered retry loop and onto the new streaming engine. Both stream=true and stream=false direct NVIDIA requests should use the same parser and engine, with different sinks.

This is the first runtime authority switch.
design: Do the direct cutover before smart-alias cutover so the new engine is battle-tested on the simpler surface first.
acceptance_criteria:
Direct NVIDIA no longer materially depends on the old buffered runtime path.
Direct stream=true requests use the streamed sink.
Direct stream=false requests use the buffered sink driven by the same parser and state machine.
Direct-route verification proves slow-success handling without premature timeout.
close_reason: Verified direct NVIDIA requests use the new streaming engine for buffered and streamed delivery, with live slow-success proof and no premature timeout.

title: Cut smart-alias NVIDIA candidates over to the streaming engine
description:
Move NVIDIA smart-alias execution and racing onto the same stream-aware engine used by direct NVIDIA requests. The smart-alias layer must respect meaningful-output lock-in, cancel loser lanes correctly, and avoid duplicate user-visible output.

This bead is the second runtime authority switch.
design: Do not leave a separate NVIDIA smart-alias buffered special case behind. The direct and smart-alias NVIDIA paths must converge on one engine.
acceptance_criteria:
executeSmartAliasMitigatedCandidate is replaced or no longer materially defines NVIDIA smart-alias runtime behavior.
Racing and failover stop once meaningful output begins.
Worker-path verification proves no duplicated tokens or tool calls under failover pressure.

title: Delete legacy NVIDIA buffered runtime code and re-verify post-deletion
description:
After the new streaming engine is authoritative for direct and smart-alias NVIDIA execution, remove the old buffered NVIDIA runtime path and any dead NVIDIA-specific deadline or retry helpers that only existed for the superseded architecture.

This bead is not complete until the old path stops materially defining runtime behavior.
design: Follow replacement sequencing strictly: cut over first, then delete, then re-verify. Do not declare completion while the old path still ships as an active route.
acceptance_criteria:
Legacy NVIDIA buffered runtime helpers are removed or inactive.
Direct and smart-alias NVIDIA both run only through the new streaming engine.
Post-deletion verification passes on specs, build, healthz, and worker preflight.

NVIDIA has a dedicated transport policy separate from generic buffered proxy requests.
